parsedVerdict.reasoning: The two services don't use the same abstractions. SchedulingService works through DAOs (PatientDao, AppointmentDao). It turns rows into domain entities (Patient, Practitioner, Appointment) and reports failures with SchedulingError. VisitNotesService skips all of that. It calls the raw PrismaService client directly (prisma.visitNote.create / findMany) instead of going through a DAO. It declares its own VisitNote data shape inside the service file rather than as an entity in src/business/entities. It also never uses the Appointment entity or SchedulingError, so it never checks that the appointmentId it receives refers to a real appointment. Inside VisitNotesService, the row-to-VisitNote mapping is written twice, once in write and once in notesFor. Together these mean the module has no single, consistent abstraction or boundary: one file is a domain service built on entities and DAOs, and the other is a thin wrapper around the ORM. The import direction itself is out of scope. What this rule covers is the inconsistent use of abstractions and the skipped persistence abstraction.

violations.message: Skips the module's persistence and domain abstractions. It uses PrismaService.visitNote directly instead of a DAO the way SchedulingService does (PatientDao/AppointmentDao), declares an ad-hoc VisitNote interface instead of a domain entity, and never checks appointmentId against the Appointment entity, so it doesn't match the rest of the module.
The row-to-VisitNote mapping ({ author, text, writtenAt }) appears twice, in write() and in notesFor(), instead of living in one place.
